anatomy.flutter: pagination.dart's own doc comment: 'page numbers, built entirely out of Button... every cell is a Button asChild wrapped around an <a>, so the pill, the spring, the focus ring and the press are the button's and are not restated.' Pagination(children) wraps a Row; PaginationLink is one numbered Button; PaginationStep.previous/.next is one widget for both chevron+word cells; PaginationEllipsis is a bare 32px Icon box.
anatomy.web: pagination.tsx exports Pagination (nav), PaginationContent (ul), PaginationItem (li), PaginationLink (Button asChild wrapping an <a>), PaginationPrevious/PaginationNext (both call PaginationLink with a chevron+span), and PaginationEllipsis (span with an Icon + sr-only text) — the same five-part anatomy the Dart doc comment names.

api.flutter: PaginationLink({label, isActive=false, onTap}); PaginationStep.previous({text='Previous', onTap}) / .next({text='Next', onTap}); Pagination({children: List<Widget>}) — takes widgets, not a model, documented as deliberate: 'the reference's own API is compositional, and a model union would be a translation of a translation.'
api.web: PaginationLink takes isActive?, disabled?, size (from Button), href, onClick, plus all native <a> props; PaginationPrevious/Next wrap it with a text? override; Pagination/PaginationContent/PaginationItem are thin div/ul/li wrappers taking standard element props — the same compositional, widget-not-model API shape.

states.flutter: PaginationLink.isActive picks ButtonVariant.outline vs .ghost, documented: 'isActive picks the variant — outline for the page you are on, ghost for the rest — and is what sets aria-current="page".' Doc comment table separately records the numbers' type drift from Previous/Next (16px/24px/500 on squares vs 13px/18.57px/500 on the word buttons) as a measured, reproduced fact, not a defect.
states.web: PaginationLink sets variant={isActive ? "outline" : "ghost"} and data-active={isActive} aria-current={isActive ? "page" : undefined} — identical rest/active state logic to the Dart file, and PaginationLink defaults size="icon" (size-10, no text-* override) versus Previous/Next's size="default", producing the same type-inheritance drift the Dart doc comment measures.

disabled.flutter: pagination.dart's PaginationLink and PaginationStep have no disabled or enabled parameter at all — onPressed is unconditionally `onTap ?? () {}`, meaning a Previous/Next cell with no onTap handler still renders as a live, pressable Button with an empty callback rather than an inert control.
disabled.web: components/ui/pagination.tsx's PaginationLinkProps carries a full disabled? implementation, documented at length in the file's own top-of-file comment: 'Handled the only way HTML allows: drop the href (which is what removes it from the tab order and from the link role's activation path), announce it with aria-disabled, pin tabindex="-1" so a stray tabindex cannot put it back, and swallow the click for a pointer that reaches it anyway.' The disabled branch also applies pointer-events-none opacity-50 via className and role="link" so the inert end of the pager stays in the accessibility tree.

ORIGINAL: This is a real, currently-shipped feature gap: the web's disabled prop and its href/tabindex/aria-disabled/preventDefault handling (added specifically to fix 'Previous on page one shipping as a fully live, focusable, clickable link that navigated nowhere' per RULES §7) has no Flutter counterpart whatsoever. Every PaginationLink/PaginationStep in pagination.dart is unconditionally interactive; a Flutter caller who wants a disabled Previous button on page one has no parameter to reach for and would have to hand-roll the IgnorePointer/opacity treatment other components (e.g. NativeSelect, MenuItem) get for free.

interaction.flutter: PaginationStep's Row lays the chevron before or after the word depending on _next, with the button's own focus ring, spring and press states inherited unchanged from Button — the doc comment states plainly 'Nothing here is a new surface... are not restated.'
interaction.web: PaginationPrevious/PaginationNext render the same chevron-before/word-first vs word-first/chevron-after ordering by composing <Icon>/<span> children into PaginationLink, which is itself `<Button asChild>` — so keyboard/pointer/focus behavior is entirely Button's own, matching the Dart file's explicit non-restatement.

semantics.flutter: PaginationEllipsis is wrapped in ExcludeSemantics, and its own doc comment states the reference ships a contradiction it reproduces rather than fixes: 'aria-hidden with an sr-only "More pages" underneath it, which is a contradiction the reference ships: aria-hidden hides the span too. The port reproduces the outcome — nothing is announced — and records the intent.' PaginationLink/PaginationStep wrap Button in Semantics(link:true, ...) with no disabled-aware label change since there is no disabled state (see disabled dimension).
semantics.web: pagination.tsx's PaginationEllipsis carries aria-hidden on the outer span with an sr-only 'More pages' span nested inside it — the same self-defeating markup the Dart doc comment calls out; separately, PaginationLink's disabled branch sets aria-disabled and role="link" specifically so a disabled pager end stays announced to assistive tech instead of disappearing from the tree.
